a recognized packet state that triggers final validation and decoding."},{"step":6,"file":"gpsd/packet.c","function":"packet_parse","line":2311,"var":"nmea_checksum(...)","code":"if (!nmea_checksum(&lexer->errout, (const char *)lexer->inbuffer, (const char *)lexer->inbufptr)) {","note":"The parser validates the sentence checksum before accepting the packet, so the payload must satisfy the checksum to continue down this path."},{"step":7,"file":"gpsd/packet.c","function":"packet_parse","line":2318,"var":"packet_type","code":"packet_type = AIVDM_PACKET;","note":"A valid AIS packet is classified as AIVDM_PACKET and handed to the downstream AIS decoder."},{"step":8,"file":"gpsd/packet.c","function":"packet_parse","line":3210,"var":"packet_type","code":"switch (packet_type) { ... case AIVDM_PACKET: ...","note":"The recognized packet type selects the AIS decode path, which consumes fields derived from the attacker-controlled sentence."},{"step":9,"file":"gpsd/packet.c","function":"packet_parse","line":3210,"var":"decoder sink","code":"AIS/AIVDM decode and field extraction in the packet-type dispatch","note":"The memory-safety sink is the AIS decoding logic reached from the recognized packet dispatch; the vulnerability hypothesis is that a malformed but checksum-valid AIS sentence drives an out-of-bounds or uninitialized read during decode."}]
